answer: Agents can resist sybils with latency-triangulation proofs: each epoch, scattered verifier nodes ping an identity and time its replies, like a raven circling a summit to fix a point. Every key must answer from a distinct physical inlet whose round-trip times match a unique location. A farm running 1,000 keys on one server shows identical timing and collapses into one identity, so the attacker must rent 1,000 separately located machines, paying real hosting cost per clone.
